The traditional fantasy setting always discuss travel between planes of existence. While this is cool and unique they hardly ever consider multiple worlds in the same universe/plane of existence.

I submit that a series of gateways, doors, portals, etc. could connect the worlds of men, elf, dragons, whatever. Each of these worlds could have some overlap in fauna and flora to ease the learning curve.

If we assume that air/atmosphere can travel between the portals you could conceivably have an ice cave in the middle of the dessert or a tropical rainforest in a mountain cave. As the gasses would flow through different worlds I would suggest having all worlds share the same general conditions, i.e. earth like.

People can barely tolerate each other and we are one species. I have a hard time believing people, dwarves, elves, etc. could all coexist in some fantasy world. This leads to a few possibilities.

Chokepoints / Limited Number of Portals - There are a fixed number of portals and they cannot easily accommodate large movements. While some worlds would have built fortresses, towns, or cities around them others may be in inaccessible mountains, barren tundra, etc. The potential for inter-world trading would be amazing.

-If you take it a step further there is no reason the portals have to line up on different worlds. Portals A & B may connect two worlds by 10 miles on Planet C while the distance on Planet D is 500 miles. This imbalance could cause great potentials for merchants, thieves, etc. The ten mile hike through the rocky fields could save a messenger several weeks or months of travel.

-These permanent portals would result in some settlement or exploration of the new world. The further a settlement is from a portal the more "local" the inhabitants would be. For instance if a cave under a remote waterfall is the entrance to the world of giants you would expect more giants or half giants to be present around this area. The locals would undoubtedly know and be familiar with giants, elves on the other hand would be a fairy tale.

Random Portals of Unknown Duration - Will daring dwellers cross through the shimmering haze and risk earning a fortune in a strange land? Will the noble scholars who hunt for arcane knowledge in the ruins of ancient worlds be lost for all times when the portal closes? Can the mages/scientists find what is causing the portals and their instability? If they can harness the portals their country would have a decisive advantage over any rival. Why were the portals originally introduced?

  1. Number of travellers per day.
  2. Weight per traveller.
  3. Type of materials, no metals, no synthetic fibers, nude?
  4. Offerings or fuel to maintain a portal?
  5. What happens if a portal suddenly closes, do items get destroyed as in the Wheel of Time?
